stages.request:
Durations are loaded as `float seconds` (`timeout = 1.5s` gives `1.5`), so our services have to multiply and round before they can use them. Make them `int milliseconds` instead: `1.5s` becomes 1500, `250ms` becomes 250, and a bare number still means seconds, so `2` becomes 2000.

A duration that doesn't come to a whole number of milliseconds, like `0.5ms` or `1.0005s`, should be rejected with `duration must be a whole number of milliseconds`.

Our deployment platform refuses environment variable names that contain a double underscore, so `LAYERCFG_SERVER__PORT` can't be set there. Switch to a single underscore between the section and the option name: `LAYERCFG_SERVER_PORT`, `LAYERCFG_POOL_MAX_SIZE`, and `LAYERCFG_SERVER_LISTEN_PORT` for the alias. Option names contain underscores themselves, so match each variable against the known option names and aliases instead of splitting it.

The double-underscore spelling goes away completely: a prefixed variable that matches no option, `LAYERCFG_SERVER__PORT` included, is reported as `unknown variable` like any other.

We want a site-wide configuration file plus a per-host file that overrides it. Change `load()` to take a list of files instead of one: `load(files=[(name, text), ...], env=...)`, each file a `(name, text)` pair. Files apply in order, so a later file overrides an earlier one, and all of them come before the environment: the layer order becomes `defaults < files in order < env`.

Each value's source still names the file and line it came from, and problems from every file are reported together. The old `file_text` and `file_name` arguments go away.

Booleans written with capitals are rejected. `debug = True` in a file, or `LAYERCFG_APP_DEBUG=YES` from our deploy script, fails with `app.debug: expected bool, got 'True'`. They should be accepted in any case, so the accepted spellings become `true/false, yes/no, on/off, 1/0 in any case`.

And when a value really isn't a boolean, the error should say what is accepted, keeping the value as it was written: `app.debug: expected bool (true/false, yes/no, on/off, 1/0), got 'maybe'`.

A typo in a key goes unnoticed: `config.get('server.prot')` quietly returns None. Looking up a key that names no option should raise `KeyError`, even when a default is passed, with a message of the form `unknown key '{key}' (did you mean '{match}'?)`, for example `unknown key 'server.prot' (did you mean 'server.port'?)`. The suggestion is the closest known key or alias; when nothing is close, leave it off and the message is just `unknown key 'zzz'`. `config['server.prot']` and `config.source('server.prot')` should fail the same way.

The `default` argument of `get` keeps a purpose: it is returned for options that exist but have no value, such as `log.file` when nothing sets it.

Two combinations of settings start the server in a broken state without any complaint. Reject them when loading: `pool.min_size` greater than `pool.max_size` (report `pool.min_size: must not exceed pool.max_size` at the place where `pool.min_size` was set; equal sizes are fine), and only one of `server.tls_cert` and `server.tls_key` being set (report `server.tls_cert and server.tls_key must be set together` at the place the one that is set came from).

Some of our hosts raise `pool.min_size` to 15, which the new check would reject against the default maximum, so raise the default `pool.max_size` from 10 to 20.
